headline: DetectifAI builds AI to detect deepfake voices on-device
summary: The startup's compact AI models aim to provide instant voice authenticity checks during calls, preventing scams before they happen.
details: Tarini Padmanabhuni founded DetectifAI after her grandfather fell victim to an AI-generated voice scam, losing money to a fake kidnapping ransom call. The incident highlighted the critical need for real-time voice authenticity verification.

AI-driven scams cost Americans nearly $900 million last year, with older adults being particularly vulnerable. DetectifAI aims to combat this growing problem by providing a defense mechanism directly on smartphones.

Unlike cloud-based detection services, DetectifAI designs compact AI models that run locally on a device. This allows for instant analysis of voice calls and messages without audio ever leaving the phone.

The company is licensing its software development kit (SDK) to phone manufacturers, positioning on-device deepfake detection as a standard feature akin to camera resolution. This strategy aims to give early adopters a competitive edge.

DetectifAI is also exploring secondary revenue streams by licensing its technology to businesses and fraud-prevention firms. The startup has already secured early revenue from financial institutions in India, handling over 100,000 calls monthly.

Padmanabhuni, who started in machine learning at age 12, has a background in cyber-physical systems and led India's first driverless racecar division in Formula Student. Her experience fuels DetectifAI's innovative approach to AI security.
The startup has received seed funding from investors like Josh Constine and is set to compete in TechCrunch's Startup Battlefield at Disrupt 2023.
